findings.evidence: Regression introduced in `pkg/util/rowcodec/encoder.go`: `Encoder.Encode(...)` now does `err := encoder.encodeRowCols(...); if err != nil { return nil, err }`, whereas first-parent code returned `encoder.row.toBytes(buf), err` (see `184b010^1:pkg/util/rowcodec/encoder.go`). This violates the stated contract used by callers (`pkg/tablecodec/tablecodec.go:EncodeRow` comment says it may return valid bytes + an error group; `EncodeOldRow` returns `valBuf` even on `flatten` error). Callers commonly do `err = sc.HandleError(err)` then proceed to persist returned bytes (e.g., `pkg/table/tables/tables.go`). Truncation-group errors can be downgraded/ignored (`pkg/sessionctx/stmtctx/stmtctx.go:newErrCtx` sets `ErrGroupTruncate` to warn/ignore based on flags), and at least one encode-time error path uses truncation codes (e.g., TIMESTAMP tz conversion can bubble `ErrWrongValue` via `pkg/types/core_time.go:CoreTime.GoTime`).
findings.fix: Restore `rowcodec.Encoder.Encode` to always return the encoded bytes alongside `err` (compute/append checksum on the produced bytes even when `err != nil`, matching the documented/old behavior), or at minimum return `encoder.toBytes(buf)` (and optionally omit checksum) instead of `nil` when `encodeRowCols` reports errors.
findings.impact: If an encode-time error is downgraded to warning/ignored by `StmtCtx.HandleError`, callers can proceed with a `nil`/empty row value, risking silent data corruption (empty record value), decode failures, and downstream consistency issues.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master` (b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943): `pkg/util/rowcodec/encoder.go` still returns `nil, err` when `encodeRowCols` returns an error.
findings.verify: Add a unit test that forces `rowcodec` encode to return a truncation-group error that can be downgraded (e.g., an invalid TIMESTAMP timezone conversion case) and assert `tablecodec.EncodeRow` returns non-nil bytes even when `StmtCtx.HandleError(err)` yields `nil`; also assert checksum bytes are appended/consistent when checksum is enabled.
findings.what: `rowcodec.Encoder.Encode` stops returning any encoded bytes when `encodeRowCols` reports errors, breaking the EncodeRow contract and creating a risk of persisting empty row values when errors are downgraded/ignored by `StmtCtx.HandleError`.

subject: rowcodec: E2E checksum introduce bytes-level checksum mechanism (#53931)
summary: The commit largely rewires row encoding to use a checksum strategy object (bytes-level CRC32) and plumbs it through table/tablecodec call sites. A High-risk regression is introduced in `rowcodec.Encoder.Encode`: it now returns `nil` bytes on encode errors, conflicting with EncodeRow’s documented behavior and potentially enabling empty-value writes if such errors are downgraded/ignored.
